England is the higher-scoring country of the two, by 2.0 runs

A first innings averages 156.6 at the 8 England grounds we hold ball-by-ball data for, across 79 matches, against 154.6 in South Africa over 103 matches. Scoring rates run 7.39 an over against 7.32. Of the countries we track, Pakistan is the highest at 172.4 and West Indies the lowest at 149.3.

Chasing costs 17.8 runs on average in England and 16.4 in South Africa — but the country average hides the spread that matters. It is 23.8 at Old Trafford, Manchester and 2.0 at Sophia Gardens, Cardiff. A total that defends comfortably at one ground is chased down at another.

How the live prediction works

It starts when the match does. There is no pre-match tip here. Win probability is recalculated after every ball from the score, wickets in hand, balls and runs remaining, and how the pitch is behaving in this innings rather than on average.

Measured, not claimed. 81.5% win-probability accuracy on a true holdout: trained on 2017-2024 matches only, then scored on 2,546 matches from 2025-26 the model had never seen, rising from 79.2% at over 6 to 82.2% by over 15.

England vs South Africa — FAQs

Is England vs South Africa higher scoring in England or South Africa?
In England. Sides batting first there average 156.6 against 154.6 in South Africa, a 2.0-run difference, and 7.39 runs an over against 7.32. Across the countries we hold ground data for, Pakistan is the highest scoring at 172.4 and West Indies the lowest at 149.3.
Which ground is hardest to chase at in this fixture?
In England it is Old Trafford, Manchester, where sides batting first average 151.0 and chasing sides 127.2 across 11 matches — a 23.8-run gap. In South Africa it is The Wanderers, Johannesburg at 40.4. The most forgiving are Sophia Gardens, Cardiff (2.0) and Newlands, Cape Town (13.0).
Who will win England vs South Africa?
We do not publish pre-match tips. The model is a live model: it has nothing useful to say until a ball is bowled, and then recalculates win probability after every one from the score, wickets in hand, required rate and how the pitch is actually playing. It measures 81.5% accuracy on a true holdout — trained on 2017-2024 matches only, then scored on 2,546 matches from 2025-26 it had never seen.
Where do these numbers come from?
Ball-by-ball T20 records for the main grounds in each country — 79 matches across 8 grounds in England, 103 across 5 in South Africa. They cover all T20 cricket at those venues, not internationals alone, so read them as ground character. Per-ground sample sizes are in the tables; some are small and deserve less weight.
